_why: The type size a person has looked at and called correct, as the median width per character, in points, of the words in print-pagebreaks.md made wholly of CJK characters (TASK-48: a CJK glyph advances by one em in every Japanese font, so this is the font size itself; the word-box height it replaced moved with the font metrics a PDF writer embeds). **Keyed by environment, not by platform**: two machines running the same OS can write the same CSS at different sizes, so a number from one is not a measurement of the other. A key with no entry is recorded and never failed — the first paper is what a baseline is made from, and only after someone opens it and says the type is right. `ci-*` keys belong to the GitHub runners; a bare platform name is a local machine's.
_required_why: Keys listed in _required must have an entry: a missing one fails the measurement instead of skipping it. That is what stops the bootstrap state — where a scaled paper passes because nothing is checking — from becoming permanent. A key goes in here at the same time as its number.
_how_to_add: Run the paper job, download the artifact, open the PDF, and only if the type is the size the print stylesheet intends, copy that run's recorded median CJK advance in here with a note saying which run it came from and what wrote the PDF (pdfinfo's Producer, and on Windows the WebView2 version in its Creator).

macos.from: the print route's own paper (task-27 paper-mac-light-7a.pdf), which is the size the print stylesheet was designed against and was accepted as such 2026-09-08; remeasured from that same PDF 2026-11-04 when the scale check moved to the CJK advance (TASK-48)
